hints.title: CAPM & beta
lines: Market risk premium = k_{M} − k_{RF}
Higher beta → higher k_{s} → lower price (same D_{1}, g)
Equilibrium: expected return = required return

hints.title: Efficient markets
lines: Weak form: past prices can't beat the market
Semistrong: public info is already in prices
Strong: even private info is in prices
Efficient ≠ all stocks have the same return (risk differs)

hints.title: Free cash flow model
lines: Firm value = PV of FCFs at WACC; horizon: FCF_{N+1} / (WACC − g)
Equity value = firm value − debt − preferred
Price per share = equity value ÷ shares

hints.title: Nonconstant growth
lines: Grow D year by year until growth is constant
P_{N} = D_{N+1} / (k_{s} − g) at the start of constant growth
P_{0} = PV of D_{1}…D_{N} + PV of P_{N}
Declining growth: use a negative g in D_{1} / (k_{s} − g)

hints.title: Preferred stock
lines: Quarterly dividends: nominal k_{p} = 4 × quarterly rate

hints.title: Yields & P/E
lines: k_{s} = dividend yield + capital gains yield = D_{1}/P_{0} + g
Constant growth: capital gains yield = g
P/E = price ÷ earnings per share

hints.title: Share counts
lines: Outstanding = issued − treasury
Can still issue (no vote needed) = authorized − issued

hints.title: Stock features
lines: Par value is symbolic, unrelated to market price
Preemptive rights protect against dilution
Preferred: fixed dividend, priority over common, usually no vote
Cumulative preferred: missed dividends must be paid first
IPO underwriter buys the shares and bears the resale risk

hints.title: Debt vs equity
lines: Debt: contractual, priority, tax-deductible interest, no vote
Equity: owners, vote, residual claim, dividends not deductible
Liquidation: secured → unsecured creditors → equity
Cost of equity > cost of debt

hints.title: Dividend policy & signals
lines: Market < intrinsic → underpriced → buy
Dividend increase = confidence; cut = possible trouble
Young, high-growth firms retain earnings
Special dividend = excess cash or unusual profit

hints.title: Dividend discount models
lines: Zero growth: P_{0} = D / r
Constant growth: P_{0} = D_{1} / (r − g), with D_{1} = D_{0}(1 + g), needs r > g
Multi-stage: PV of early dividends + PV of P_{N} = D_{N+1} / (r − g_{long})

hints.title: Growth & PVGO
lines: SGR = ROE × (1 − payout ratio)
No-growth value = EPS / r (or D / r if all earnings are paid out)
PVGO = price − no-growth value; negative = growth destroys value

hints.title: Stock basics
lines: P_{0} = PV of all expected future dividends
Constant growth: P_{0} = D_{1} / (r − g), r > g

questions.question: Which feature belongs to DEBT rather than equity?
choices: Voting rights in electing directors
Ownership of the firm and its profits
A contractual duty to pay interest
A residual claim on assets
Dividends paid at the board's discretion

questions.question: If a firm fails and its assets are sold, in what order are the proceeds paid out?
choices: Equity holders, then unsecured creditors, then secured creditors
Secured creditors, then unsecured creditors, then equity holders
Unsecured creditors, then equity holders, then secured creditors
Everyone is paid equally
Equity holders first, since they own the firm

questions.question: Which payment is tax-deductible for the firm?
choices: Dividends to common shareholders
Dividends to preferred shareholders
Interest paid to debt holders
Share buybacks
None of them
questions.explanation: Interest is deducted before taxes (EBIT − interest = taxable income). Dividends are paid from after-tax income.

questions.question: Which is generally higher: the cost of debt or the cost of equity?
choices: Cost of debt, because interest payments are fixed by contract
Cost of equity, because equity is riskier and not tax-deductible
They are always equal in a well-run, efficient market
Cost of debt, because lenders are paid before shareholders
It can't be compared, since equity has no stated rate
questions.explanation: Debt is less risky (contractual, priority) and interest is tax-deductible, so equity costs more.

questions.question: The par value of common stock is:
choices: Its current market price
Mostly symbolic and unrelated to market value
The dividend the company pays on each share every year
The price set at the IPO
The book value of equity divided by shares outstanding

questions.question: John owns 50,000 of a firm's 100,000 shares. The firm issues 50,000 new shares to outsiders. What protection would have let John keep his 50% stake?
choices: A two-for-one stock split
Preemptive rights
A proxy statement
Cumulative preferred dividends
Buying back treasury shares
questions.explanation: Without preemptive rights John drops to 50,000/150,000 = 33% (dilution of ownership). Preemptive rights let existing holders buy new shares first.

questions.question: A firm has 55,000,000 authorized shares, has issued 20,000,000, and holds 1,000,000 in treasury. How many shares are outstanding?
questions.explanation: Outstanding = issued − treasury = 20M − 1M = 19M.

questions.question: Same firm: 55,000,000 authorized, 20,000,000 issued, 1,000,000 treasury. How many more shares can it issue without shareholder approval?
questions.explanation: Authorized − issued = 55M − 20M = 35M.

questions.question: Why might founders create super-voting (multiple votes per share) stock?
choices: To pay higher dividends to the founders
To keep control and block hostile takeovers
To lower the firm's corporate tax rate
To make the shares cheaper for new buyers
To avoid having to issue bonds later
questions.explanation: Different share classes (e.g. Google's A/B/C) keep voting control with founders and defend against takeovers or proxy fights.

questions.question: Google's GOOG (Class C) shares carry:
choices: 1 vote per share
10 votes per share
No voting rights
Guaranteed dividends
Preferred status
questions.explanation: GOOGL (A) = 1 vote, Class B = 10 votes, GOOG (C) = no votes.

questions.question: A proxy is:
choices: A short-term bond issued by the firm
Written permission to vote for a shareholder
A dividend paid in extra shares of stock
A share the company holds in its treasury
The registration document for an IPO

questions.question: You own 100 shares and the firm declares a 5% stock dividend. You receive:
choices: $5 in cash
5 additional shares
50 additional shares
Nothing
$0.50 per share

questions.question: Which is NOT a typical feature of preferred stock?
choices: A fixed periodic dividend
Priority over common stock in dividends and liquidation
Normally no voting rights
Unlimited voting power over the board
May be convertible into common shares

questions.question: A firm skips two years of dividends on its CUMULATIVE preferred stock. Before paying common dividends again, it must:
choices: Pay nothing extra to the preferred holders
Pay all the missed preferred dividends first
Convert the preferred shares into common
Issue new bonds to the preferred holders
Get approval from the common shareholders
questions.explanation: Cumulative: unpaid dividends accumulate and must be paid before common holders get anything. Non-cumulative: missed dividends are lost.

questions.question: Wealthy individuals who invest their own money in early-stage firms for equity, without operating as a business, are called:
choices: Venture capitalists
Angel investors
Investment bankers
Hedge fund managers
Underwriters

questions.question: In an IPO, the investment bank that underwrites the offering:
choices: Lends the firm money at a fixed interest rate
Buys the shares and bears the risk of reselling them
Guarantees investors a minimum return on the shares
Takes deposits from investors before the offering
Sets the firm's dividend policy after the IPO

questions.question: A stock trades at $40, but your valuation says its intrinsic value is $50. The stock is:
choices: Overpriced, so sell
Underpriced, so buy
Fairly priced
Worthless
Impossible to judge

questions.question: Perry Motors just paid a $1.80 dividend. The required return is 12%. If dividends never grow, what is the stock worth?
Perry Motors just paid a $1.80 dividend. The required return is 12% and dividends grow at 5% forever. What is the stock worth?
Sweet Candy will pay a $0.72 dividend next year and grow 7% per year forever. What is the stock worth at a 10% required return?
questions.explanation: P₀ = D₁ / (r − g) = 0.72 / 0.03 = $24.00. (Next year's dividend is already D₁, so don't grow it again.)

questions.question: Sweet Candy ($0.72 next dividend, 7% growth) is worth $24 at r = 10%. What is it worth at r = 8%, and what does that show?
choices: $9.00; the model barely reacts to r
$72.00; the model is very sensitive to r
$24.00; the value doesn't depend on r
$36.00; growth no longer matters here
Undefined; r has to equal g for it to work
questions.explanation: 0.72 / (0.08 − 0.07) = $72. A 2-point change in r tripled the value: the Gordon model is very sensitive to r − g, and r must exceed g.

questions.question: A stock just paid a $2.00 dividend, which will grow 6% per year forever. The required return is 11%. What is it worth?
A stock sells for $40, will pay a $2.00 dividend next year, and dividends grow at 5% per year. What return do investors require?
A preferred share pays a fixed $5 dividend forever. The required return is 8%. What is it worth?
questions.explanation: Preferred stock = a perpetuity (zero-growth model): 5 / 0.08 = $62.50.

questions.question: Warren Industries' last dividend was $1.50. Dividends grow 10% per year for 3 years, then 5% per year forever. The required return is 15%. What is the stock worth?
A stock just paid $1.00. Dividends grow 20% for 2 years, then 5% forever. The required return is 12%. What is it worth?
Home Place Hotels paid $3.40 last year. Growth: 0% next year, 5% in years 2 and 3, 15% in year 4, then 10% forever. At a 14% required return, what is the maximum price per share?
questions.explanation: D₁ = 3.40, D₂ = 3.57, D₃ = 3.75, D₄ = 4.31, D₅ = 4.74. P₄ = 4.74 / (0.14 − 0.10) = $118.55. Discounting everything back at 14% gives $81.00.

questions.question: Perry Motors just paid $1.80. Dividends grow 5% for 3 years, then 4% forever. The required return is 12%. What is the stock worth?
DTE Energy had an ROE of 10%, EPS of $4.05 and a dividend of $2.35. What is its sustainable growth rate?
A firm has an ROE of 15% and pays out 40% of its earnings as dividends. What is its sustainable growth rate?
questions.explanation: SGR = ROE × (1 − payout) = 15% × 60% = 9%.

questions.question: Alpha Manufacturing pays $4 per share (all earnings), r = 12%, and the market price is $30. What is its PVGO?
questions.explanation: No-growth value = 4 / 0.12 = $33.33. PVGO = 30 − 33.33 = −$3.33: investors think its growth plans will earn less than 12%.

questions.question: A stock trades at $70, its EPS is $5, and the required return is 10%. What is the present value of its growth opportunities?
questions.explanation: No-growth value = EPS / r = 5 / 0.10 = $50. PVGO = 70 − 50 = $20.

questions.question: A negative PVGO suggests:
choices: The firm should reinvest an even larger share of earnings
Reinvesting destroys value, so paying out may be better
The stock is effectively risk-free at its current price
The firm has no debt and should borrow to grow faster
The dividend must be cut immediately to save cash

questions.question: A firm announces a dividend INCREASE. The market usually reads this as:
choices: A sign the firm is in financial trouble
Confidence in future earnings and cash flow
A warning that bankruptcy is coming soon
Nothing at all; investors ignore dividends
A plan to issue more debt in the near term

questions.question: Which firm is MOST likely to pay a low dividend?
choices: A mature utility with stable, predictable earnings
A young firm with many profitable investment projects
A firm with no new investment needs at the moment
A firm with very high liquidity and no debt at all
A firm in a boom year that has built large reserves
questions.explanation: New firms retain earnings for growth; firms with profitable opportunities are justified in retaining earnings.

questions.question: A one-time special dividend most likely signals that the firm:
choices: Is close to bankruptcy and returning what it can
Has excess cash it can't reinvest well right now
Will raise its regular dividend every year from now on
Needs to borrow money to fund its next project
Is preparing to go public with an IPO soon

questions.question: An increase in a firm's expected growth rate would normally cause the firm's required rate of return to
choices: Increase.
Decrease.
Fluctuate.
Remain constant.
Possibly increase, possibly decrease, or possibly remain unchanged.

questions.question: If the expected rate of return on a stock exceeds the required rate,
choices: The stock is experiencing supernormal growth.
The stock should be sold.
The company is probably not trying to maximize price per share.
The stock is a good buy.
Dividends are not being declared.

questions.question: Stock A has a required return of 10 percent. Its dividend is expected to grow at a constant rate of 7 percent per year. Stock B has a required return of 12 percent. Its dividend is expected to grow at a constant rate of 9 percent per year. Stock A has a price of $25 per share, while Stock B has a price of $40 per share. Which of the following statements is most correct?
choices: The two stocks have the same dividend yield.
If the stock market were efficient, these two stocks should have the same price.
If the stock market were efficient, these two stocks should have the same expected return.
Statements a and c are correct.
All of the statements above are correct.
questions.explanation:
The total return is made up of a dividend yield and capital gains yield.
For Stock A, the total required return is 10 percent and its capital gains
yield (g) is 7 percent. Therefore, A's dividend yield must be 3 percent.
For Stock B, the required return is 12 percent and its capital gains yield
(g) is 9 percent. Therefore, B's dividend yield must also be 3 percent.
Therefore, statement a is true. Statement b is false. Market efficiency
just means that all of the known information is already reflected in the
price, and you can't earn above the required return. This would depend on
betas, dividends, and the number of shares outstanding. We don't have any
of that information. Statement c is false. The expected returns of the
two stocks would be the same only if they had the same betas.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is most correct?
choices: The constant growth model takes into consideration the capital gains earned on a stock.
It is appropriate to use the constant growth model to estimate stock value even if the growth rate never becomes constant.
Two firms with the same dividend and growth rate must also have the same stock price.
Statements a and c are correct.
All of the statements above are correct.
questions.explanation:
Statement a is true; the other statements are false. The constant growth
model is not appropriate for stock valuation in the absence of a constant
growth rate. If the required rate of return differs for the two firms due
to risk differences, then the firms' stock prices would differ.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is most correct?
choices: The stock valuation model, P0 = D1/(ks - g), can be used for firms which have negative growth rates.
If a stock has a required rate of return ks = 12 percent, and its dividend grows at a constant rate of 5 percent, this implies that the stock's dividend yield is 5 percent.
The price of a stock is the present value of all expected future dividends, discounted at the dividend growth rate.
Statements a and c are correct.
All of the statements above are correct.
questions.explanation:
Statement a is true; the other statements are false. If a stock's
required return is 12 percent and its capital gains yield is 5 percent,
then its dividend yield is 12% - 5% = 7%. The expected future dividends
should be discounted at the required rate of return.

questions.question: A stock's dividend is expected to grow at a constant rate of 5 percent a year. Which of the following statements is most correct?
choices: The expected return on the stock is 5 percent a year.
The stock's dividend yield is 5 percent.
The stock's price one year from now is expected to be 5 percent higher.
Statements a and c are correct.
All of the statements above are correct.
questions.explanation:
Statement c is true; the others are false. Statement a would be true only
if the dividend yield were zero. Statement b is false; we've been given
no information about the dividend yield. Statement c is true; the
constant rate at which dividends are expected to grow is also the expected
growth rate of the stock's price.

questions.question: Stocks A and B have the same required rate of return and the same expected year-end dividend (D1). Stock A's dividend is expected to grow at a constant rate of 10 percent per year, while Stock B's dividend is expected to grow at a constant rate of 5 percent per year. Which of the following statements is most correct?
choices: The two stocks should sell at the same price.
Stock A has a higher dividend yield than Stock B.
Currently Stock B has a higher price, but over time Stock A will eventually have a higher price.
Statements b and c are correct.
None of the statements above is correct.
questions.explanation:
Statement a is false: P0 = D1/(ks - g). g is different for the two stocks,
but the required return and expected dividend are the same, so the prices
will be different also. Statement b is false: ks = D1/P0 + g. A has a
higher g, so its dividend yield must be lower because the firms have the
same required rate of return. Statement c is false. Therefore, statement
e is the correct answer.

questions.question: Stock X and Stock Y sell for the same price in today's market. Stock X has a required return of 12 percent. Stock Y has a required return of 10 percent. Stock X's dividend is expected to grow at a constant rate of 6 percent a year, while Stock Y's dividend is expected to grow at a constant rate of 4 percent. Assume that the market is in equilibrium and expected returns equal required returns. Which of the following statements is most correct?
choices: Stock X has a higher dividend yield than Stock Y.
Stock Y has a higher dividend yield than Stock X.
One year from now, Stock X's price is expected to be higher than Stock Y's price.
Statements a and c are correct.
Statements b and c are correct.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is statement c.

For Stock X, ks = D1/P0 + g
                      0.12 = D1/P0 + 0.06, or D1/P0 = 0.06.

For Stock Y, ks = D1/P0 + g
                      0.10 = D1/P0 + 0.04, or D1/P0 = 0.06.

So, both Stock X and Stock Y have the same dividend yield. So, statements a
and b are incorrect. That also makes statements d and e incorrect. Since both
stocks X and Y have the same price today, and Stock X has a higher dividend
growth rate than Stock Y, the price of Stock X will be higher than the price
of Stock Y one year from today. So, statement c is the correct choice.

questions.question: Stock X is expected to pay a dividend of $3.00 at the end of the year (that is, D1 = $3.00). The dividend is expected to grow at a constant rate of 6 percent a year. The stock currently trades at a price of $50 a share. Assume that the stock is in equilibrium, that is, the stock's price equals its intrinsic value. Which of the following statements is most correct?
choices: The required return on the stock is 12 percent.
The stock's expected price 10 years from now is $89.54.
The stock's dividend yield is 6 percent.
Statements a and b are correct.
All of the statements above are correct.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is statement e. At a price of $50, ks = D1/P0 + g =
$3.00/$50 + 0.06 = 12%. So, statement a is correct. P^10 = $50(1.06)10 =
$89.54. So, statement b is also correct. D1/P0 = $3.00/$50.00 = 6%, so

statement c is correct. Thus, statement e is the correct choice.

questions.question: Stock X has a required return of 12 percent, a dividend yield of 5 percent, and its dividend will grow at a constant rate forever. Stock Y has a required return of 10 percent, a dividend yield of 3 percent, and its dividend will grow at a constant rate forever. Both stocks currently sell for $25 per share. Which of the following statements is most correct?
choices: Stock X pays a higher dividend per share than Stock Y.
Stock X has a lower expected growth rate than Stock Y.
One year from now, the two stocks are expected to trade at the same price.
Statements a and b are correct.
Statements a and c are correct.
questions.explanation:
If Stock X has a required return of 12 percent and a dividend yield of
5 percent, we can calculate its growth rate:

 ks = D1/P0 + g
12% = 5% + g

 7% = g.

If Stock Y has a required return of 10 percent and a dividend yield of
3 percent, we can calculate its growth rate:

 ks = D1/P0 + g
10% = 3% + g

 7% = g.

Since both stocks have the same price and Stock X has a higher dividend yield
than Stock Y, its dividend per share must be higher. Therefore, statement a
is true. We just showed above, that both stocks have the same growth rate, so
statement b must be false. One year from now, the stocks will both trade at
the same price. They are starting at the same price today, and will be
growing at the same rate this year, so they will end up with the same stock
price one year from now. Therefore, statement c must also be true. Since
both statements a and c are true, the correct choice is statement e.

questions.question: Stock A has a beta of 1.1, while Stock B has a beta of 0.9. The market risk premium, kM - kRF, is 6 percent. The risk-free rate is 6.3 percent. Both stocks have a dividend, which is expected to grow at a constant rate of 7 percent a year. Assume that the market is in equilibrium. Which of the following statements is most correct?
choices: Stock A must have a higher dividend yield than Stock B.
Stock A must have a higher stock price than Stock B.
Stock B's dividend yield equals its expected dividend growth rate.
Statements a and c are correct.
All of the statements above are correct.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is statement a. From the information given and the
CAPM equation, we know that Stock A's and Stock B's required returns are
12.9% and 11.7%, respectively. The required return is equal to a dividend
yield and a capital gains yield. Since these are constant growth stocks,
their capital gains yields are equivalent to their dividend growth rates
of 7%. Therefore, the dividend yields for Stock A and Stock B are 5.9%
and 4.7%, respectively. Statement b is incorrect; we cannot determine
which stock has the higher price without knowing their expected dividends.

 Statement c is incorrect; from the answer given for statement a, we know
that Stock B's dividend yield doesn't equal its expected dividend growth
rate.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is most correct?
choices: If a company has two classes of common stock, Class A and Class B, the stocks may pay different dividends, but the two classes must have the same voting rights.
An IPO occurs whenever a company buys back its stock on the open market.
The preemptive right is a provision in the corporate charter that gives common stockholders the right to purchase (on a pro rata basis) new issues of common stock.
Statements a and b are correct.
Statements a and c are correct.
questions.explanation:
Statement c is true; the others are false. Two classes of common stock
can have different voting rights, as well as pay different dividends.
An IPO occurs when a firm goes public for the first time. Statement c is
the exact definition of a preemptive right.

questions.question: The preemptive right is important to shareholders because it
choices: Allows management to sell additional shares below the current market price.
Protects the current shareholders against dilution of ownership interests.
Is included in every corporate charter.
Will result in higher dividends per share.
The preemptive right is not important to shareholders.

questions.question: Companies can issue different classes of common stock. Which of the following statements concerning stock classes is most correct?
choices: All common stocks fall into one of three classes: A, B, and C.
Most firms have several classes of common stock outstanding.
All common stock, regardless of class, must have voting rights.
All common stock, regardless of class, must have the same dividend privileges.
None of the statements above is necessarily true.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is most correct?
choices: If a market is strong-form efficient this implies that the returns on bonds and stocks should be identical.
If a market is weak-form efficient this implies that all public information is rapidly incorporated into market prices.
If your uncle earns a return higher than the overall stock market, this means the stock market is inefficient.
Statements a and b are correct.
None of the above statements is correct.
questions.explanation:
Statements a through d are false; therefore, statement e is true.

Statement a is false. Strong-form efficiency states that current market

prices reflect all pertinent information, whether publicly available or

privately held. If it holds, even insiders would find it impossible to

earn abnormal returns in the stock market. Statement b is false; this

describes semistrong-form efficiency.  Statement c is false; some

investors may be able to analyze and react more quickly than others to

releases of new information. However, the buy-sell actions of those

investors quickly bring market prices into equilibrium.

questions.question: Assume that the stock market is semistrong-form efficient. Which of the following statements is most correct?
choices: Stocks and bonds should have the same expected returns.
In equilibrium all stocks should have the same expected returns, but returns on stocks should exceed returns on bonds.
You can expect to outperform the overall market by observing the past price history of an individual stock.
For the average investor, the expected net present value from investing in the stock market is zero.
For the average investor, the expected net present value from investing in the stock market is the required return on the stock.
questions.explanation:
Stocks are usually riskier than bonds and should have higher expected
returns. Therefore, statement a is false. In equilibrium, stocks with
more market risk should have higher expected returns than stocks with less
market risk. Therefore, statement b is false. The semistrong form of
market efficiency says that all publicly available information, including
past price history, is already accounted for in the stock's price.
Therefore, statement c is false. Remember, when trying to find the price
of a stock, we discount all future cash flows by the required return. If
the price is equal to the present value of those cash flows, then the NPV
of the stock must be equal to 0. Therefore, statement d is true. Net
present value is stated in dollars and the required return is stated as a

percent. It is impossible for the two to equal each other. Therefore,

statement e is false.

questions.question: Assume that the stock market is semistrong-form efficient. Which of the following statements is most correct?
choices: The required rates of return on all stocks are the same and the required rates of return on stocks are higher than the required rates of return on bonds.
The required rates of return on stocks equal the required rates of return on bonds.
A trading strategy in which you buy stocks that have recently fallen in price is likely to provide you with returns that exceed the rate of return on the overall stock market.
Statements a and c are correct.
None of the statements above is correct.
questions.explanation:
Statement a is false; riskier securities have higher required returns.
Statement b is false for the same reason as statement a. Statement c is
false; semistrong-form efficiency says that you cannot make abnormal
profits by trading off publicly available information. So statement e is
the correct answer.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is most correct?
choices: If the stock market is weak-form efficient, then information about recent trends in stock prices would be very useful when it comes to selecting stocks.
If the stock market is semistrong-form efficient, stocks and bonds should have the same expected return.
If the stock market is semistrong-form efficient, all stocks should have the same expected return.
Statements a and c are correct.
None of the statements above is correct.
questions.explanation:
Weak-form efficiency means that you cannot profit from recent trends in
stock prices (that is, technical analysis doesn't work). Therefore,
statement a must be false. Semistrong-form efficiency means that all
public information is already accounted for in the stock price. Because
bonds and stocks have different risk levels and tax implications, there is
no reason to expect them to have the same return. Therefore, statement b
must be false. Similarly, because different stocks have different risk
levels, there is no reason to expect all stocks to have the same return.
Therefore, statement c is also false. The correct choice is statement e.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is most correct?
choices: Semistrong-form market efficiency implies that all private and public information is rapidly incorporated into stock prices.
Market efficiency implies that all stocks should have the same expected return.
Weak-form market efficiency implies that recent trends in stock prices would be of no use in selecting stocks.
All of the statements above are correct.
None of the statements above is correct.
questions.explanation:
Statement c is true; the other statements are false. Semistrong-form
market efficiency implies that only public information, not private, is
rapidly incorporated into stock prices. Markets can be efficient yet
still price securities differently depending on their risks.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is most correct?
choices: Semistrong-form market efficiency means that stock prices reflect all public information.
An individual who has information about past stock prices should be able to profit from this information in a weak-form efficient market.
An individual who has inside information about a publicly traded company should be able to profit from this information in a strong-form efficient market.
Statements a and c are correct.
All the statements above are correct.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is most correct?
choices: If a market is weak-form efficient, this means that prices rapidly reflect all available public information.
If a market is weak-form efficient, this means that you can expect to beat the market by using technical analysis that relies on the charting of past prices.
If a market is strong-form efficient, this means that all stocks should have the same expected return.
All of the statements above are correct.
None of the statements above is correct.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is statement e. If prices rapidly reflect all
available public information, then the market is semistrong-form efficient
not weak-form efficient. Therefore, statement a is incorrect. If the
market is weak-form efficient, then you cannot beat the market by using
technical analysis or charting. Therefore, statement b is incorrect.
Different stocks will have different risk and will have different required
and expected returns, so statement c is incorrect.

questions.question: Most studies of stock market efficiency suggest that the stock market is highly efficient in the weak form and reasonably efficient in the semistrong form. On the basis of these findings which of the following statements is correct?

Information disclosed in companies' most recent annual reports can be used to consistently beat the market.

questions.explanation:
Statement a is true; the other statements are false. Historical
information cannot be used to beat the market under weak-form efficiency.

 Public information cannot be used to beat the market under semistrong-
form efficiency.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is most correct?

One of the advantages of common stock financing is that a firm's debt ratio will decrease.
Statements b and c are correct.
All of the statements above are correct.
questions.explanation:
Statements b and c are true; therefore, statement d is the correct choice.
A greater proportion of common stock in the capital structure increases
the likelihood of a takeover bid.

questions.question: Stock X has a required return of 10 percent, while Stock Y has a required return of 12 percent. Which of the following statements is most correct?
choices: Stock Y must have a higher dividend yield than Stock X.
If Stock Y and Stock X have the same dividend yield, then Stock Y must have a lower expected capital gains yield than Stock X.
If Stock X and Stock Y have the same current dividend and the same expected dividend growth rate, then Stock Y must sell for a higher price.
All of the statements above are correct.
None of the statements above is correct.
questions.explanation:
We don't know anything about the dividends of either stock. Stock Y could
have a dividend yield of 0 percent and a capital gains yield of 12
percent, while Stock X has a dividend yield of 10 percent and a capital
gains yield of 0 percent. Therefore, statement a is false. If the two
stocks have the same dividend yield, Stock Y must have a higher expected
capital gains yield than X because Y has the higher required return.
Therefore, statement b is false. Remember the DCF formula: P0 = D1/(ks -
g). If D1 and g are the same, and we know that Y has a higher required
return than X, then Y's dividend yield must be larger than X's. In order
for this to be true Y's price must be lower than X's. Therefore,
statement c is false. Since statements a, b, and c are false, then the
correct answer is statement e.

The stock with the higher dividend yield will have a higher dividend growth rate.
questions.explanation:
ks = D1/P0 + g. Both stocks have the same ks and the same P0, but may have

questions.question: Stocks A and B have the same price, but Stock A has a higher required rate of return than Stock B. Which of the following statements is most correct?

If Stock A has a lower dividend yield than Stock B, its expected capital gains yield must be higher than Stock B's.
If Stock A has a higher dividend yield than Stock B, its expected capital gains yield must be lower than Stock B's.
Stock A must have both a higher dividend yield and a higher capital gains yield than Stock B.
questions.explanation:

both a dividend yield (D1/P0) and a growth rate. Statements a and b don't
mention the growth rate. Statement c is true because if the required
return for Stock A is higher than that of Stock B, and if the dividend
yield for Stock A is lower than Stock B's, the growth rate for Stock A
must be higher to offset this. Statement d is not necessarily true
because the growth rate could go either way depending upon how high the
dividend yield is. Statement e is also not necessarily true.

questions.question: If markets are in equilibrium, which of the following will occur:
choices: Each investment's expected return should equal its realized return.
Each investment's expected return should equal its required return.
Each investment should have the same expected return.
Each investment should have the same realized return.
All of the statements above are correct.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is statement b. The realized return is an historical

return. It is what has already happened in the past. There is no reason

that the expected return in the future should equal the return it has

realized in the past. Therefore, statement a is incorrect. If the

expected return does not equal the required return, then markets are not

in equilibrium. If you are expecting a higher return than you require

(given the level of risk) for a stock, then the stock will be a "bargain."

You will be getting a higher return than you require.  This

disequilibrium will not last, and the stock price will adjust until its

expected return equals its required return. Therefore, statement b is

correct. Different investments should have different expected returns.

You will have a different expected return for an oil company stock than

you would for an airline company stock, depending on what is happening to

oil prices. There is no reason for you to expect the same returns on all

of your investments. Therefore, statement c is incorrect. Investments

should not have the same realized returns. Realized returns are

historical, and all stocks have different price histories. Therefore,

statement d is incorrect.
